records.name: Charlie Perkins Scholarship
records.program_type: Charitable trust scholarship (Indigenous Australians, study in the United Kingdom)
records.description: The Charlie Perkins Scholarship Trust funds Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians to undertake full-time postgraduate study at the University of Oxford or the University of Cambridge. Each award covers up to three years of full university and college fees, travel costs and an annual stipend of GBP 20,810 for 2025-2026. Applications open in early October and close at the end of January each year, so the window is open now.
records.application_period: Scholarship applications open at the beginning of October to the end of January each year
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent, identify as such and be accepted by their community, supply written confirmation of Indigenous identity from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council, and be applying for or enrolled in a full-time postgraduate course at Oxford or Cambridge.
eligibility: Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent, and identify as such and be accepted in the community where the applicant lives or has lived
Written confirmation of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander identity from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council
Written confirmation of enrolment in a postgraduate course at the University of Oxford or the University of Cambridge
Full-time postgraduate study at Oxford or Cambridge only
A budget (template provided) showing how the scholarship funds will be used
Ability to demonstrate how the chosen course of study will support leadership in the applicant's field and communities
coverage: Full university and college fees for up to three years
Travel costs to and from the United Kingdom
Annual stipend to cover living expenses
benefits: Up to three years of full university and college fees at Oxford or Cambridge
Annual living stipend (GBP 20,810 for the 2025-2026 academic year)
Advice and support from the Trust, and connections with current scholars
requirements: Register interest with the Trust by email to discuss the application and college choice
Apply to the University of Oxford and/or the University of Cambridge and be accepted in order to receive the scholarship
Submit a personal statement of no more than two pages
Submit a completed budget using the Trust's template
required_documents: Personal statement of no more than two pages
Written confirmation of full-time enrolment, or of the university application submitted
Official transcript of university results including mid-year results if available
Signed statement of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council
Completed budget using the Trust's template
Written reference from an Elder or senior community member
Two additional academic references, or one academic and one professional reference
application_method: Register interest with the Trust by email
Apply directly to the University of Oxford and/or the University of Cambridge
Submit the scholarship application and all supporting documents to the Trust before the closing date
records.english_requirement: Not stated as a separate requirement; study is at Oxford or Cambridge, so English ability is implied by the admissions requirement.
records.selection_notes: A panel of prominent Indigenous and non-Indigenous Australians, together with a representative of the British Government and Cambridge Australia Scholarships, selects the scholars each year. Applications missing any required document are not considered complete and do not pass the shortlisting stage.
records.best_fit: An Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Australian with a completed or nearly completed undergraduate degree, applying to Oxford or Cambridge for 2027 entry, who intends to lead in their field and community.
records.notes: Award value varies with the holder's course. Oxford application fees are GBP 75 per course and Cambridge GBP 65 per application; applicants are encouraged to apply to both. PhD writing-up periods are not automatically funded.

official_details.application_cycle: Annual cycle; scholarship applications open at the beginning of October and close at the end of January, so the window is open on 2026-10-04
official_details.deadline_note: The Trust publishes a recurring window only: "Scholarship applications open at the beginning of October to the end of January each year." No exact calendar date is published for the 2027 entry cycle, so deadline_date is null. Oxford and Cambridge also impose their own course-level admissions deadlines, which the Trust says applicants must check separately, including the Cambridge Graduate Funding deadline.
official_details.status_note: The published application window (beginning of October to end of January) is current on 2026-10-04. Applicants must also meet Oxford or Cambridge admissions deadlines for 2027 entry, which are set by the universities and fall earlier.
official_details.funding_duration: Up to three years of fees, travel and stipend
official_details.tuition_coverage_note: The Trust states the award covers "up to three years' full university and college fees" at Oxford or Cambridge.
official_details.funding_label: Fully funded: up to three years of full university and college fees, travel costs and an annual stipend of GBP 20,810 (2025-2026). Must be accepted by Oxford or Cambridge. No bond or service obligation is published.
benefits: Up to three years of full university and college fees at Oxford or Cambridge
Travel costs to and from the United Kingdom
Annual stipend covering living expenses, GBP 20,810 for the 2025-2026 academic year
Trust advice, current-scholar connections and application support
eligibility: Be of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent
Identify as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander and be accepted as such by the community in which the applicant lives or has lived
Provide written confirmation of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander identity from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council
Provide written confirmation of enrolment in a postgraduate course at the University of Oxford or the University of Cambridge
Provide a budget, using the Trust template, outlining how the scholarship funds will be used
Demonstrate how the chosen course of study will support leadership in the applicant's field and communities
Be accepted by the University of Oxford or the University of Cambridge in order to receive the scholarship
official_details.citizenship_residency: Not published as a citizenship test; eligibility is defined by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent and community acceptance.
official_details.international_eligibility: Open to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians only. The award is for study in the United Kingdom, not in Australia.
official_details.application_method: Three steps: register interest with the Trust by email to discuss the application and college choice; apply for admission to the University of Oxford and/or the University of Cambridge, nominating two participating colleges each; then submit the scholarship application and all required documents to the Trust.
official_details.application_route: Applications are submitted to the Charlie Perkins Scholarship Trust, with the form hosted on the Aurora Indigenous Pathways Portal; the Trust's own page directs applicants to the Aurora Indigenous Pathways Portal to apply.

Apply to Oxford and/or Cambridge and be accepted in order to receive the scholarship; a scholarship application may be made while the university application is under consideration
Submit a personal statement of no more than two pages covering community connection and past contributions, motivation for the course, and how the course supports leadership
Submit a completed budget using the Trust's template
Nominate two participating colleges when applying to Oxford or Cambridge
Pay the university application fee: GBP 75 per course at Oxford, GBP 65 per application at Cambridge (non-refundable)
documents: Written confirmation of full-time enrolment from the relevant university, or written confirmation that the university application has been submitted
Official transcript of university results, including mid-year results if available
Signed statement of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council

Two additional references: either two academic references, or one academic and one professional reference
official_details.english_requirement_note: The Trust states no separate English-language requirement. Because the award is tenable only at Oxford or Cambridge, applicants must meet those universities' English admission requirements.
selection_criteria: Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent and acceptance by the applicant's community
Potential to become a leader in the field of study and in the applicant's communities
Quality of the two-page personal statement
A completed budget showing how the funds will be used
Complete submission of every required document; incomplete applications do not pass shortlisting
award_holder_conditions: Must be accepted by the University of Oxford or the University of Cambridge to receive the scholarship

application_readiness_checklist: Register interest with the Trust by email early, to discuss the application and college choice
Choose your Oxford and/or Cambridge course and check that university deadline first; Oxford course deadlines vary and are often much earlier than the Trust's January closing date
Secure written confirmation of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander identity from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council
Obtain written confirmation of full-time enrolment, or of the university application submitted
Draft a two-page personal statement covering community connection, motivation and leadership
Build the budget on the Trust's own template
Line up an Elder or senior community member for a reference, plus two academic references or one academic and one professional reference
Book a professional high resolution JPEG headshot
common_rejection_risks: Missing any single required document; the Trust states an incomplete application is not considered complete and does not pass the shortlisting process
Missing the Oxford or Cambridge admissions deadline even though the Trust window is still open
Identity confirmation that does not come from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council
An academic reference supplied by professional rather than academic staff; the Trust will not accept it
A personal statement longer than two pages
An award amount assumed to cover living costs beyond the published annual stipend, or a PhD writing-up period assumed to be funded
estimated_uncovered_costs: Oxford application fees of GBP 75 per course and Cambridge application fees of GBP 65 per application
Any living costs above the published annual stipend of GBP 20,810
Visa costs, immigration health surcharge and any Oxford or Cambridge college-specific charges not met by the award
An optional PhD writing-up period, which the Trust states is not automatically funded
document_audit: Full-time enrolment letter, or confirmation that the university application was submitted
Official transcript of results including mid-year results where available
Signed Indigenous identity confirmation from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council
Completed budget on the Trust template
Reference from an Elder or senior community member
Two additional references, academic or mixed academic and professional as permitted

alerts.message: Scholarship applications open at the beginning of October each year and close at the end of January, so the scholarship side of the application is open now, on 2026-10-04.

Oxford and Cambridge set their own course deadlines, and the Trust tells applicants to apply before the Cambridge Graduate Funding deadline. Work backwards from the university deadline, not from January.
You must be accepted by Oxford or Cambridge to receive the scholarship. A scholarship application alone does not secure the award.
The Trust states the award value varies with the course of study and quotes GBP 20,810 for 2025-2026. Do not assume the same figure for a later entry year.

submission_workflow: Email the Trust to register interest and discuss college choice
Research Oxford and Cambridge course entry requirements and their individual application deadlines
Apply to the chosen courses, nominating two participating colleges at each university
Obtain the Indigenous identity confirmation letter from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council
Request the Elder or community reference and the two additional references from academic or professional referees
Complete the budget on the Trust template and assemble the full document set
Submit the scholarship application through the Aurora Indigenous Pathways Portal before the closing date
